title: Lounger #23 Reference-Graph Persistence and Control-Binding Audit

gate.question: Does the public shipped-data reference graph expose a unique persistent child, linked reference, token, alias, container or storage object reachable from James's Lounger #23 endpoint that can serve as a James-specific persisted-state candidate?
gate.passed: Lounger terminals are persistent/quest-bound objects whose displayed state is conditioned by MQ04 quest state, and James's Lounger #23 has a distinct terminal and Dad-specific NOTE set inside the shared Think Machine/Braun control domain.
gate.open: No unique James-specific storage child, linked reference, carrier object, session token, container or persistent memory handle was identified in the publicly indexed raw ESM material reviewed.
gate.effect: The persistence/control plane is established, but the storage/carrier edge remains unresolved.

terminal.description: LOUNGER #23 MONITOR STATION / RESIDENT ID: UNKNOWN

pod_script.finding: OnActivate only blocks/conditions player interaction and exposes no storage, linked-reference, carrier or memory-operation call.

terminal_record_flags.finding: Raw terminal records for Vault 112 loungers are flagged Quest item / Persistent reference.
terminal_record_flags.significance: The monitor class participates in persistent quest/control state rather than being a transient UI-only object.

quest_condition_binding.finding: Resident-status/stress menu entries switch between normal and dead NOTE records using MQ04 quest variables such as Invasion.
quest_condition_binding.significance: Lounger monitor output is coupled to persistent MQ04 control state.

james_specific_storage_child.finding: No publicly indexed raw record reviewed exposed a unique object reachable specifically from Vault112PodTermDad that stores James memory or session state.

think_machine_3600r.finding: The Think Machine 3600r runs the main simulation and synchronizes all Tranquility loungers.

per_lounger_subsystems.finding: The central mainframe appears linked to smaller computers, one handling each lounger's graphics processing and occupant medical status.

visiontron_boundary.finding: The lounger processes user input locally while the actual simulation runs through a connected processing center such as the Think Machine 3600r.

central_backend_context.implication: The most plausible persistence search surface is the per-lounger subsystem / central backend boundary, not the static Dad monitor NOTE records.

resident_id_boundary.rule: Do not equate James with Dithers or Resident ID 642 without direct ESM reference binding; transcript variants conflict.

save_james_effect.improvement: James's Lounger #23 endpoint is now explicitly anchored inside a persistent MQ04-controlled monitor class, narrowing the unresolved search to backend storage rather than endpoint identity.
save_james_effect.reason: No unique storage/session/carrier object was resolved from the public reference graph.
